description: Section ENR 4.1 of the United States Aeronautical Information Publication, issued by the Federal Aviation Administration, describes the radio navigation aids used en route. Contents: for each system (nondirectional beacons, VOR, DME, TACAN, VORTAC, localiser and landing aids, GPS, WAAS, GBAS) it gives frequency bands, such as 190 to 535 kHz for NDBs and 108.0 to 117.95 MHz for VORs, line-of-sight and service volume limits, accuracy, identification and known interference sources, and it explains the VOR Minimum Operational Network kept as a backup for GPS outages, GPS testing NOTAMs with affected radii, reporting of GNSS interference and the end of LORAN-C in 2010. Coverage: the US national airspace system. Format and access: HTML pages and a PDF edition of the AIP, updated with each amendment. Licence and cost: free federal publication. Caveats: a narrative reference, not a station list; facility locations and frequencies are in the NASR data. Useful for modelling navigation coverage and the loss of GNSS in aviation resilience studies, including space weather and jamming scenarios. It relates to the FAA NASR aeronautical data and the GLA maritime GNSS study in the catalogue.
